consequential_owner_action.action: owner-signed mandate authorization admission for slot 'owner/default' (schema openline.mandate_owner_authorization.v1)
consequential_owner_action.discrimination: ACTIVE admits governing authority; REVOKED is the owner STOP. Acceptance = the receiver's admit() decision; the effect boundary = mandate-head admission.
gate_checks_preregistered: correct action binding (mandate_hash binds the pinned mandate)
current standing (sequence/predecessor continuity on the current head)
valid signature/proof (Ed25519 against the CURRENTLY pinned owner key)
correct consequence (receiver status follows the admitted record: ACTIVE or REVOKED)

current_owner_definition: the last entry of the slot's key schedule (genesis = receiver-configured pinned key; advanced only by admitted succession events). current_owner() returns {owner_id, public_key}.
do_not: build recovery UX, multisig, social recovery, generic PKI, or redesign Wallet
repair CI or the baseline test file inside this experiment
downstream_checks_preregistered: CI-equivalent: unittest discovery with pytest import blocked (classify the pre-existing baseline failure separately; reproduce on clean baseline main)
exact_success_condition: PASS only if every bounded-case expectation holds on every receiver it names, the appraiser re-derives all expectations from frozen evidence (zero VIOLATIONs), all downstream suites pass with no new failures and no rewritten prior PASS evidence, and: owner-issued consequential authority is accepted when current (case 1); worker credentials cannot mint or impersonate owner authority (case 2); succession advances B to current through the preregistered trust path (case 3); successor B exercises current owner authority (case 4); superseded A cannot authorize new consequential actions (case 5); cryptographic validity of an old credential does not restore current standing (case 5 evidence); restart/reload preserves B as current (case 6); historical receipts remain verifiable across succession without conferring currency (case 7); existing Receiver Gate / Wallet / STOP / succession / distributed-STOP / effect-closure invariants remain intact; no existing PASS receipt is rewritten to make the experiment succeed.

exact_succession_rule_under_test.atomicity_rule: exactly one current owner root per slot at all times. Admit advances the single pinned key; historical keys remain in the schedule for verification only. No accepted state where old and new are both CURRENT.
exact_succession_rule_under_test.authoritative_transition_rule: the A->B succession event becomes authoritative for a receiver when admitted via MandateOwnerView.admit_trust_root_succession (persistence-before-decision inside the trust-root DurableHeadStore). Convergence is per-receiver admission, not broadcast.
exact_succession_rule_under_test.monotonic_sequence: succession_sequence must equal previously admitted sequence + 1 (first event: 1)
exact_succession_rule_under_test.no_op_forbidden: successor_public_key must differ from the current pinned key
exact_succession_rule_under_test.predecessor_binding: predecessor_succession_hash must equal payload_hash of the previously admitted succession event (null for the first)
exact_succession_rule_under_test.primitive: the shipped in-band succession mechanism in olp_gate/mandate_owner.py, used exactly as-is; zero product-code changes
exact_succession_rule_under_test.signer_rule: event must be signed by the CURRENTLY pinned owner key (observed signer key == expected current key); a successor can never install itself
exact_succession_rule_under_test.supersede_binding: event.owner_id must equal the current owner_id (the transition supersedes the current owner, not a third party)

failure_condition: FAIL on the first tested path that allows: a model/worker/session to exercise owner-only consequence authority without the owner trust path (case 2 acceptance); old owner A to authorize a new consequence after B is authoritative (case 5 acceptance); restart resurrecting A's current standing (case 6); recovery creating two simultaneously current owners where this preregistration requires one; B becoming current without current-owner authorization; historical verification requiring A to be current; succession destroying or rewriting historical evidence; or the mechanism failing to distinguish valid signature from current standing.
forbidden_semantic_changes_after_contact: the claim itself; no rescue reruns under this label
historical_verification_requirement: A-era receipts must remain attributable and verifiable as historical facts (verified=True, current=False, historical-key reason code) without A becoming current again; assess() must first validate against the current root and only then fall back to superseded roots.
implementation: harness-only. No product-code changes. Reuses the proven succession_worker.py receiver process (unchanged), a new case driver (7 bounded cases), a new independent appraiser, and new in-process unit tests. Zero product-code changes is the plan; if implementation proves required, the smallest change necessary, disclosed, with semantics frozen here.
narrow_claim_tested: THE OWNER HOLDS THE KILL AUTHORITY, AND SUCCESSION DOES NOT GIVE THE OLD HOLDER POWER BACK.
owner_trust_anchor: receiver-pinned Ed25519 owner key per mandate slot. Slot 'owner/default', owner_id 'owner'. Genesis root = key A, pinned in receiver configuration (not self-naming: the mandate cannot promote its own signer).

receipt_distinctions.ACCEPTED: receiver admit() returned admitted=True (all gate checks passed; head advanced).
receipt_distinctions.AUTHORIZED_FOR_THIS_ACTION: signer key == currently pinned owner key at admission time (the owner-key standing check). The authority boundary.
receipt_distinctions.CURRENT_OWNER: the single pinned root = last schedule entry, as reported by MandateOwnerView.current_owner().
receipt_distinctions.EFFECTED: head state changed to the admitted record's state and persisted (receiver standing follows: ACTIVE governs, REVOKED = STOP).
receipt_distinctions.HISTORICALLY_VALID: record validates fully under a superseded (scheduled) root: the signature was valid and the root was current when the receipt was created; the root is not current now.
receipt_distinctions.SIGNATURE_VALID: Ed25519 signature verifies against the claimed signer's public key (olp_gate.crypto.verify_olp_signature). Pure cryptography; says nothing about authority.

receipt_evidence_per_case: case 1: A ACTIVE seq1 + REVOKED seq2 signed bodies, admission records both receivers, status transitions
case 2: W-signed REVOKED seq3 signed body, refusal records both receivers (reason code), head snapshots showing no movement
case 3: A->B succession event (signed body, payload_hash, signature), admission records both receivers, post-admission status snapshots
case 4: B ACTIVE seq3 + REVOKED seq4 + ACTIVE seq5 signed bodies, admission records both receivers
case 5: A-signed REVOKED seq6 signed body, independent SIGNATURE_VALID verification record, refusal records both receivers, head snapshots
case 6: restart boundary: pre/post status snapshots of R1, durable store files, B ACTIVE seq6 admission on R1, A ACTIVE seq7 refusal on R1
case 7: assess() records for A-era and B-era receipts on R2
global: keys.json (public keys A,B,C,W), mandate.json, run_log.jsonl, per-receiver admissions journals, snapshots, case_results.json
topology: one owner driver (holds keys A genesis owner, B successor, C third party, W non-owner worker; issues all records) + two independent receiver worker OS processes (R1, R2), each with its own state dir (durable mandate heads, durable trust-root succession store, admissions journal). File inbox/command protocol; no in-process double-calling. Restart = terminate R1, respawn from durable state only (--init not passed).
